title: Text & Structure
subtitle: Core Markdown syntax for readable notes and runbooks

commands.details: Use one # heading for the document title, then descend one level at a time. A space after the # characters is required by CommonMark. Keep a blank line around headings for portability.

commands.cmd:
First paragraph.

Second paragraph.

Line one  
Line two
commands.details: A blank line starts a new paragraph. Two trailing spaces make a hard line break, but are easy to miss in review; use separate paragraphs when possible.
Use ** for strong emphasis, * for emphasis, and backticks for literal commands, paths, identifiers, and output. Keep punctuation outside code spans unless it is part of the literal text.

commands.cmd:
\*literal asterisks\*
\# not a heading
Use `*` for a wildcard
commands.details: Backslash escapes punctuation in normal Markdown text. An inline code span is often clearer for syntax characters. Backslashes do not escape content inside fenced code blocks.

commands.cmd:
- Check BMC SEL
- Capture GPU telemetry

1. Identify the failed device
2. Map BDF to physical slot
commands.details: Use a blank line before a list following a paragraph. Start each item with a marker and a space. Numbered lists express sequence; bullets group peers.
Indent child bullets beneath the parent item, typically two spaces for a one-character bullet marker. Keep indentation consistent to avoid unexpected list structure.

commands.cmd:
- [x] Capture SEL
- [x] Map GPU UUID to BDF
- [ ] Inspect physical module
- [ ] Attach logs to ticket
commands.details: Task checkboxes are a GitHub Flavored Markdown extension, not core CommonMark. Use x for checked and a space for unchecked. Rendering and editability vary by platform.

title: Links & Images
subtitle: Point to evidence and keep paths reviewable

commands.details: Relative links work within a repository when the destination moves with it. Reference links keep long URLs out of prose. Check whether the target viewer supports local paths.
Alt text should describe the image's useful content. A relative image path is resolved from the Markdown file. Do not embed credentials or sensitive labels in images before sharing.
Angle brackets make explicit autolinks in CommonMark. Bare URLs are recognized by some renderers, including GitHub Flavored Markdown, but are less portable.

title: Code & Evidence
subtitle: Preserve exact commands and diagnostic output

commands.details: Put the opening and closing fences on their own lines. The language hint enables syntax highlighting where supported. A Markdown code fence shows text; it never executes it.
Use text for raw output so highlighting does not reinterpret it. Keep timestamps, device identifiers, and error wording intact when recording evidence; sanitize credentials before sharing.

commands.desc: Quote an observation or ticket excerpt
commands.cmd:
> Technician observed link LED dark on OSFP cage 4.
> No cable swap performed yet.
commands.details: The > marker distinguishes quoted source material from your own diagnosis. Attribute the source and time in surrounding prose when they matter.
Three hyphens on their own line make a thematic break. Leave blank lines around it. Use headings for structure; use rules sparingly.
Tables are a GitHub Flavored Markdown extension. The separator row is required; colons set left, center, or right alignment. Tables are best for short single-line cells.

commands.cmd:
~~Suspected cable fault~~
Confirmed transceiver fault after A/B swap.
commands.details: Strikethrough with ~~ is a GitHub Flavored Markdown extension. For incident records, state when and why a conclusion changed rather than relying on strikethrough alone.

commands.desc: Add a footnote when the renderer supports it
commands.cmd:
BER exceeded the site threshold.[^threshold]

[^threshold]: See the local fabric acceptance criteria.
commands.details: Footnotes are supported by GitHub and some other renderers, but are outside core CommonMark. Use a plain link or nearby note when portability matters.

title: GitHub Features
subtitle: Renderer-specific tools for longer technical notes

commands.desc: Call out a note or warning in GitHub
commands.cmd:
> [!NOTE]
> Link counters were sampled after the cable swap.

> [!WARNING]
> Obtain approval before resetting the GPU.
commands.details: GitHub alert syntax is not core CommonMark. Other viewers may show it as an ordinary block quote. Keep the key instruction in the text itself.

commands.desc: Collapse a long log excerpt on GitHub
commands.details: GitHub supports HTML details and summary elements. Blank lines around the Markdown block inside are needed for reliable rendering. Some viewers sanitize or ignore inline HTML.

commands.desc: Draw a small path diagram where Mermaid is supported
commands.details: Mermaid diagrams render on GitHub and some other platforms, but are not part of CommonMark. Include a text description when the path must remain clear in plain-text viewers.

commands.desc: Link to a heading in the same document
commands.details: GitHub creates heading fragments from heading text. Fragment rules differ among renderers and duplicate headings can get numbered suffixes; test links in the target viewer.

title: Incident Templates
subtitle: Reusable structure for case notes and runbooks

commands.cmd:
# Incident: node-a GPU 3

## Symptom

## Safety state
- Scheduler: drained / active / unknown
- GPU processes: none / present / unknown

## Evidence
- GPU UUID / BDF / physical module:
- Timestamped logs:

## Hypothesis and next action

## Timeline
commands.details: Record exact identifiers, timestamps, and safety state before proposing intrusive diagnostics. Use unknown until verified; do not present placeholders as findings.

commands.cmd:
# Procedure: replace OSFP module

## Scope and prerequisites

## Safety and approval checks

## Steps
1. Record port and transceiver IDs.
2. Capture baseline telemetry.

## Verification

## Rollback and escalation
commands.details: A runbook should name the target, prerequisites, approval point, expected result, and rollback. The sample is only an outline; it does not authorize physical or network changes.

commands.desc: Add YAML metadata for a supporting tool
commands.cmd:
---
title: GPU NVLink triage
owner: datacenter-ops
status: draft
---

# GPU NVLink triage
commands.details: YAML front matter is a convention used by static site generators and note apps, not core Markdown. Check the receiving tool's schema and quote values when YAML syntax requires it.

commands.desc: List headings in a Markdown file
commands.details: A quick plain-text outline. This can also match headings inside fenced code blocks; use a Markdown-aware parser if exact structure matters.

commands.desc: Lint Markdown with an installed CLI
commands.details: Run when markdownlint-cli2 is installed. Its rules depend on local configuration; fix or intentionally configure reported style issues before publishing.

commands.desc: Convert Markdown to HTML with Pandoc
commands.details: Requires Pandoc. This writes summary.html and may not reproduce every GitHub feature exactly. Review the output and avoid rendering untrusted HTML in privileged contexts.

commands.desc: Show a fenced block inside Markdown documentation
commands.details: Use an outer fence with more backticks than any inner fence. This preserves literal Markdown examples in a document without prematurely closing the outer block.
